scams.name: La Pavona Pirate Boat Fare Inflation
scams.tldr: The pivot lands the moment you climb out of a Caribe Shuttle van or step off the Cariari–Pavona minibus with a suitcase.
scams.description: The pivot lands the moment you climb out of a Caribe Shuttle van or step off the Cariari–Pavona minibus with a suitcase. A man in an unmarked polo waves you over before you can read the schedule board. He says the next public boat is full or canceled and his boat leaves now. There is no signage in English, no posted price list, and the dirt path to the river crossing is a gauntlet of similar offers.
scams.avoidance: Buy public boat tickets at the official window inside the La Pavona restaurant building. Verify the schedule at pavonatortuguero.com before you arrive at the dock. Refuse to pay more than 4,000 CRC per person each way for the public boat. Ignore anyone in an unmarked shirt who approaches your shuttle van. Photograph the posted parking sign before you hand over keys.
scams.location: La Pavona dock, Cariari minibus stop, Guápiles bus station, La Pavona parking lot, Tortuguero town dock

scams.name: Shadow Turtle Nesting Walk
scams.tldr: The pitch lands at dusk on the muddy main street between Aracari Garden Hostel and the soccer field, where guides loiter by the public phone and hostel boards.
scams.description: The pitch lands at dusk on the muddy main street between Aracari Garden Hostel and the soccer field, where guides loiter by the public phone and hostel boards. He says he grew up here, that his cousin is a ranger, that the official tours are sold out for the night. He waves a white flashlight, not a red one — the first technical tell.
scams.avoidance: Book the turtle walk through your hotel or the Sea Turtle Conservancy office. Ask to see the guide's SINAC photo ID badge before you leave the meeting point. Confirm the assigned beach sector at the Cuatro Esquinas ranger station. Refuse to walk the nesting beach with anyone using a white flashlight. Verify the Sea Turtle Conservancy fee at conserveturtles.org before paying cash.
scams.location: Tortuguero village beach, north of the lighthouse, Sea Turtle Conservancy gate, Cuatro Esquinas ranger station, hotel lobbies on Main Street

scams.name: Canal Tour Cash Markup at the Dock
scams.tldr: The encounter starts the moment you step off the Pavona boat with a daypack still on your shoulders.
scams.description: The encounter starts the moment you step off the Pavona boat with a daypack still on your shoulders. A man with a clipboard and a laminated wildlife photo asks if you want to see sloths and caimans, says the next park boat leaves in fifteen minutes, names a price in dollars only. The pitch is timed for tired arrivals.
scams.avoidance: Book canal and kayak tours through your hotel or an ASOPROTUR-affiliated operator. Pay the $15 SINAC park entry online at sinac.go.cr before arrival. Confirm the guide is a certified naturalist before you board. Refuse cash-only US-dollar tours quoted on the public dock. Compare the dock price to hotel rates of $25 to $35 before you commit.
scams.location: Tortuguero village dock, Main Street tour booths, Cuatro Esquinas park entrance, hotel package desks, Sea Turtle Conservancy footpath

scams.name: Fake Park Conservation Fee Collector
scams.tldr: He has no printed receipt book and never enters the rangers' kiosk.
scams.description: He has no printed receipt book and never enters the rangers' kiosk. The move plays on friction in the official process: SINAC switched to advance online tickets at sinac.go.cr a few years ago, the website is clunky, and many travelers arrive at the trailhead unsure whether they paid the right thing.
scams.avoidance: Buy Tortuguero National Park tickets at sinac.go.cr before you travel. Show the SINAC QR confirmation email to the ranger at the kiosk. Refuse any cash request outside the official rangers' booth. Photograph the SINAC fee schedule before you reach the gate. Report fake collectors to the rangers at Cuatro Esquinas immediately.
scams.location: Cuatro Esquinas ranger station, Jalova trailhead, Tortuguero village dock, Sea Turtle Conservancy footpath, beach access trails

scams.name: Jungle Lodge Last-Night Room Theft
scams.tldr: The pattern mirrors the rising property-crime trend the US Embassy in San José flagged in its Nov.
scams.description: The pattern mirrors the rising property-crime trend the US Embassy in San José flagged in its Nov. 26, 2025 security alert. The set-up is the lodge layout itself. Rooms sit on raised stilts along jungle walkways, doors are often louvered for airflow, and all-inclusive packages mean guests are out for hours-long boat tours and group dinners.
scams.avoidance: Use the in-room safe for cash, watches, passports, and electronics on every tour. Photograph the safe's contents and your room's door on check-in. Carry the spare passport copy in a money belt under clothing. Request a deposit-box receipt at the front desk for valuables. Repack the night before departure and lock everything in the safe again.
scams.location: Mawamba Lodge, Pachira Lodge, Tortuga Lodge, Aracari Garden Hostel, hotel boat-transfer docks
